title.narrative: EU-China Think-Tank Engagement: The art of realising Tianxia ¿ EU and China under one heaven (ARTEUCH project)

description.narrative: Contract related to: EU-China Think-Tank Engagement: The art of realising Tianxia ¿ EU and China under one heaven (ARTEUCH project) - The EU-China bilateral relation is one of the most important and complex in the global system of international relations, with profound implications across economy, society, democracy, human rights, global governance, science and the health of our environment. The EU & China Think-Tank Engagement project, as a public diplomacy tool, enables the EU to engage meaningfully on a long-term basis with Chinese civil society actors, paying a particular focus on think-tanks and academia. By doing so, the action increases mutual understanding, improves the perception of the EU and its policies among target actors and stirs cooperation with like-minded partners, thus supporting the implementation of EU Foreign Policy objectives. Sustained and effective engagement with think-tanks and expert audiences in both the EU and China enhances the knowledge, understanding and perception regarding the fundamental mechanisms and procedures that govern the EU and its Member States, supports the EU to better understand Chinese dominant perspectives and, ultimately, builds trust, secures channels for open dialogue and creates networks of partnerships at the level of civil society actors and academia.Therefore, the proposed action aims to support the European Union, represented by the EU Delegation to China, in its endeavour to enhance EU-China dialogue at the level of civil society actors ¿ in particular think tanks and academia, setting the stage for intensified bilateral relations and advancing the EU¿s policy priorities in China. The following fields of action are envisaged: 1. Enhance the capacity of the EU Delegation to China to undertake constant and long-term engagement with influential think-tanks and academic institutions, thus creating networks of partnerships.2. Improve the understanding about EU¿s positions on shared global concerns among Chinese academia, international relations experts and wider audiences, thus bridging perception gaps.3. Maintain open channels for honest and meaningful dialogue between representatives of academia and think tanks in China and the EU, thus increasing mutual trust and understanding.
